operations.evidence: The April 2024 to February 2026 occurrence window and rolling recall design were recorded.
The occurrence window was not labelled as a single incident year or police-recording period.
The national 989,000 violence-with-or-without-injury survey estimate for people aged 16 and over was recorded.
The survey estimate was not represented as a police count or parcel-level rate.
The absence of a statistically significant annual change was recorded with survey-uncertainty context.
No significant change was not converted to zero change or a local conclusion.
Redeveloped CSEW sexual-victimisation questions and their measurement-improvement purpose were recorded.
Questionnaire redevelopment retained mandatory measure-version metadata.
The latest sexual-victimisation estimates were recorded as non-comparable with previous published measures.
Old and new measures were forbidden from a continuous trend without an official bridge.
Later-2026 publication of domestic-abuse and stalking estimates after additional QA and analysis was recorded.
Deferred values were not inferred or converted to zero.
The updated combined domestic-abuse sexual-victimisation and stalking measure was recorded as deferred until later in 2026.
The previous combined value was not relabelled or recomputed as the March 2026 estimate.
Domestic abuse sexual victimisation stalking and harassment were preserved outside CSEW headline crime.
Headline crime was not represented as all victimisation and separate denominators were retained.
The sample-not-population design and resulting uncertainty were recorded.
Point estimates were not treated as precise counts and non-sampling error remained possible.
The current 2 April 2026 QMI revision and its methodology role were recorded.
The QMI revision date was not substituted for an observation date.
Quarterly crime outputs combining survey and administrative sources were recorded.
Quarterly publication was not applied to every component and source types remained separate.
The 43 territorial forces plus BTP monthly Home Office-to-ONS aggregation chain was recorded.
The aggregation chain was not treated as direct parcel evidence.
Verian's formally accredited quality systems and scripting-to-data-checking protocols were recorded.
Contractor accreditation was not treated as removal of sampling or nonresponse uncertainty.
ONS final-preparation and publication quality-management controls were recorded.
Publication QA was not represented as exact local validation or error-free data.
The 9 June 2026 crime-methodology hub and its guide note and questionnaire links were recorded.
The hub was treated as an index and linked documents retained separate revisions.
The 5 June 2026 revision of the March 2025 user guide was recorded.
Title year and revision year were kept separate and release-specific caveats remained required.
Police recorded crime was preserved as official statistics without accredited designation.
Non-accredited status was not equated to unusable data and fitness remained offence-specific.
CSEW accredited-official-statistics status and independent OSR review were recorded.
Accreditation was not treated as removal of sampling uncertainty or universal output coverage.
The current HTML release ODS tables technical annex and user-engagement assets were recorded as an edition-matched bundle.
Narrative and data assets were not mixed across editions or treated as the same analytical object.
Official source rows 451-470 were published in two bounded files with explicit limitations and no candidate derivation.
Official source rows 471-490 were published in two bounded files with current ONS and Home Office edition metadata.
Operation rows 1099-1182 preserve separate validation and limitation entries for website line-by-line visibility.

All 12 candidates remain unjoined at confidence zero; source rows 451-490 and operation rows 1099-1182 were published without a second runner, task, candidate value, business row, database write, migration or deployment.
